signIn.title: Sign-in
signIn.noProvider: No single sign-on provider is enabled yet – only administrators would be able to sign in. Configure one under Users & teams.
signIn.question: Who may sign in with a password?
signIn.fromEnv: Set on the server with <c>{{name}}</c> – change it there.
signIn.pendingNone: <c>{{name}}=none</c> takes effect once an administrator has signed in with single sign-on. Until then administrators sign in with their password – so this installation can be set up.

mode.allHint: Users sign in with a local password or, if configured, with single sign-on.
mode.adminsOnly: Single sign-on, administrators also with a password
mode.adminsOnlyHint: Everyone signs in with single sign-on. Local administrator accounts can still use their password as break-glass access.
mode.noneHint: Nobody signs in with a password. If the identity provider fails, an administrator gets in with emergency access from the server's command line.

signIn.noneNeedsProvider: Single sign-on only needs an enabled single sign-on provider (Users & teams).
signIn.noneNeedsSsoAdmin: To turn on single sign-on only, sign in with single sign-on as an administrator first – then you know that at least one administrator can still get in.
signIn.emergencyHint: If single sign-on fails, run <c>steward admin emergency-access</c> with an administrator's user name on the server. It needs the data folder and the master passphrase, and prints a one-time sign-in link. Keep both available to at least two people.
signIn.sessionsEnd: When you save, password sessions this setting no longer allows are signed out. API tokens keep working.

confirm.adminsOnly: Only administrators will be able to sign in with a password. Other people's password sessions are signed out now.
confirm.none: Nobody will be able to sign in with a password. Password sessions are signed out now, and password resets are no longer possible. If single sign-on fails, only emergency access from the server's command line gets you in.

language.title: Language
language.defaultHint: For messages posted to a channel (Microsoft Teams, webhook) and for people who have not chosen a language yet.
language.hint: Everyone picks their own language in the user menu or on their profile; in-app notifications and e-mails use it. Audit entries and the messages of runs stay in English.

browser.title: Browser automation
browser.missing: Playwright is not installed. Run <c>npm install</c> and <c>npx playwright install chromium</c>, then restart.
browser.headlessHint: Turn off to watch the browser while a process runs (useful when building browser steps).
browser.tip: Tip: <c>npx playwright codegen https://your-portal</c> records clicks and shows selectors you can paste into browser steps.

outbound.title: Outbound access
outbound.platformsHint: Processes may reach the origins of configured platforms (and their trusted origins) and the allow-list below. Recommended.
outbound.allowListHint: Processes may reach only the destinations on the allow-list below – not even configured platforms unless listed.
outbound.openWarning: Processes may reach any host. Only use this in a lab. Cloud-metadata and link-local addresses and the server's own port stay blocked.
outbound.listHint: One entry per line: an origin (https://host[:port]), a host or host glob (*.example.com) or a CIDR. Cloud-metadata (169.254.169.254, …) and link-local addresses and the Steward server's own port are always blocked.
outbound.note: Absolute URLs that are not covered here fail with a message telling the author to ask an administrator to allow the origin.
outbound.whenNeeded: Do I need an entry? Built-in connector reads (repositories, Kubernetes, Prometheus …) and connection tests go to the platform's own address – no. Process steps, access reviews, endoflife.date, Gatus scrapes and the MCP gateway may reach configured platforms with “Configured platforms + allow-list”. Monitor HTTP checks, webhooks, SBOM URLs and Git sync need an entry for hosts that are no platform; TCP/ping checks and Zabbix always do. With “Allow-list only” nothing is implicit. Details: docs/SECURITY-HARDENING.md.

problems.path: an origin has no path – use https://host[:port]
problems.cidr: use an IPv4 CIDR such as 10.10.13.0/24
problems.port: the port must be between 1 and 65535
problems.host: not a host name, IP address or origin – one entry per line

compliance.title: Access reconciliation
compliance.dismissFourEyesHint: A finding someone dismisses stays open until a second person (the owner of the check or an administrator) confirms the dismissal.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.runsHint: Includes logs and evidence files. 0 = forever. New installations start with 400 days.
retention.hint: Older runs, read notifications and monitor history are deleted automatically. The audit log is never pruned.
retention.monitorsHint: Status changes, uptime samples and check results of monitors.
retention.debugRunsHint: Debug runs (one node, step through) are deleted after this many days (1–90), before the other runs. Their audit entries stay.
retention.debugPauseHint: A paused step-through run is stopped after this many minutes (1–240).

unattended.title: Unattended operation
unattended.intro: Schedules only run while the vault is unlocked; scheduled runs use the rights of the person who owns the schedule. These options are part of the server configuration and take effect when Steward starts.

unlocked.label: Start unlocked after a reboot
unlocked.hint: For example as a Windows service: keep the master passphrase in a file only the service account can read – not in a user environment variable, which every program would inherit.

network.label: Use over the network
network.hint: Let colleagues open Steward from their computers: listen on all network interfaces and name the host name they use.

https.label: HTTPS
https.hint: Encrypt the connection with your certificate and its key.

backup.label: Back up the data directory
backup.hint: It contains the database, encrypted credentials, evidence files and the audit log.

maintenance.confirm: Delete runs and notifications older than the saved retention periods now? This cannot be undone.
maintenance.cleanupHint: Uses the saved retention periods. Cleanup also runs automatically.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.hint: Tokens of all users. Users create their own tokens on their profile page.
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke the token “{{name}}” of {{owner}}? Scripts using it stop working immediately.

notify.willBeRemoved: Will be removed when you save.
notify.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Tests use the saved settings, so save first.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.intro: How people are told about failed runs, waiting decisions and more. In-app notifications appear under the bell.
notify.baseUrlHint: Used for links in e-mails and Teams messages, e.g. {{example}}
notify.secureHint: On for port 465. Off uses STARTTLS when the server offers it.
notify.teamsUrlHint: Incoming webhook or Workflows “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received” URL
notify.webhookUrlHint: Receives a JSON POST per notification (e.g. ticketing, Slack, automation)
notify.routesHint: Each event goes to the people it concerns. E-mails are only sent to users who turned e-mail notifications on in their profile.
notify.allowedDomains: Allowed e-mail domains for addresses outside Steward
notify.allowedDomainsHint: Credential owners and report recipients that are not Steward users only get e-mails at these domains, e.g. corp.example or *.corp.example (all subdomains). Empty: the domains of the Steward users’ own addresses (used by an administrator, a single sign-on account or at least two users).
notify.passwordAgain: The server, port, user or TLS changed: enter the password again (the stored one is never sent to another server or without TLS).

publicApi.title: REST API
publicApi.off: The REST API (<c>{{path}}</c>) is turned off on this server.
publicApi.baseUrl: REST API base URL: <c>{{url}}</c> (read-only, OpenAPI 3.1, version {{version}})
publicApi.docsAccess: Who can open the API documentation
publicApi.docsFromEnv: Set by the environment variable <c>{{name}}</c> on the server.
publicApi.docsHint: Who may open the interactive documentation (Swagger UI) and the OpenAPI document without a token. The API itself always needs an API token (created on the profile page).
publicApi.docsHintRateLimit_one: Who may open the interactive documentation (Swagger UI) and the OpenAPI document without a token. The API itself always needs an API token (created on the profile page) and allows {{count}} request per minute and token.
publicApi.docsHintRateLimit_other: Who may open the interactive documentation (Swagger UI) and the OpenAPI document without a token. The API itself always needs an API token (created on the profile page) and allows {{count}} requests per minute and token.

vault.title: Master passphrase
vault.hint: Changing the passphrase re-wraps the vault's keys. With "rotate the data key", every stored credential is also re-encrypted with a new key, so an old vault.json together with the old passphrase opens nothing current. The audit chain and its signing key stay the same.
vault.nextHint: At least {{count}} characters – a sentence of several words works well
vault.rotate: Rotate the data key (re-encrypt all credentials)
vault.rotateHint: Recommended when the old passphrase or a backup of vault.json may have been exposed
vault.tooShort: The passphrase needs at least {{count}} characters
vault.backupHint: Back up the new vault.json together with the database. Update SM_MASTER_PASSPHRASE_FILE (unattended start) as well.

dailySummary.title: Daily summaries
dailySummary.description: People turn the daily summary on in their profile. Here you can stop it for everyone and see who receives one (not what it contains). E-mail goes only to addresses in the allowed domains, and only while the event "Daily summary" is routed to e-mail above.
dailySummary.none: Nobody receives a daily summary yet.

migration.title: Migration
migration.card: Move this instance to another one – for example from the desktop app to a server with PostgreSQL and single sign-on – or bring a moved instance in, with a mapping of every user and team.
migration.intro: Export a migration package of this instance, or import one from another instance. Everything important moves: data, stored files and the audit log. Every user and team of the package is mapped to an account and team here, and the mapping is recorded in the audit log.

export.title: Export this instance
export.intro: Writes one file with all data, stored files and the audit log. It is encrypted with a transfer passphrase and signed with this instance's key. Credentials are encrypted again for the target. Sessions, API tokens and the sign-in setup do not move.
export.passphraseHint: The package carries every credential, so the master passphrase is asked again.
export.transferHint: At least {{count}} characters. The target needs it to open the package – pass it on separately from the file.
export.ready: {{rows}} rows in {{tables}} tables, {{files}} files and {{entries}} audit entries – {{size}}.
export.undecryptable_one: {{count}} credential could not be decrypted here and is moved empty.
export.undecryptable_other: {{count}} credentials could not be decrypted here and are moved empty.
export.once: The download works once, within 30 minutes. Note the fingerprint: the target shows it for confirmation.

import.title: Import a package
import.intro: Into a new instance: set up the administrator and single sign-on first. The package is checked before anything changes (dry run).
import.fingerprintLabel: Fingerprint of the source's signing key
import.fingerprintHint: Read it on the source, not here: the source showed it when it exported the package (also under Audit log → Anchoring outside the database → Signing key fingerprint). Enter all {{min}} characters; the colons are optional.
import.doneText: {{rows}} rows, {{files}} files and {{entries}} audit entries of the source are here now.
import.temporaryPasswords: One-time passwords of the new local accounts (shown once):

plan.title: Dry run
plan.migrations_one: {{count}} database migration is applied on import.
plan.migrations_other: {{count}} database migrations are applied on import.
plan.paused: Imported paused (turn them on after a review): {{list}}.
plan.notApplied: Settings of the source that are not applied

mapping.usersHint: Decide for every user of the source what they are here. Ownership and access move with the decision; the history keeps the source's names and shows who they are now.
mapping.clash: An account "{{name}}" exists here: map to it, or the name would mean two people.
mapping.ssoHint: Exactly the user name single sign-on gives (e.g. the e-mail / UPN); linked at the first sign-in.
mapping.confirmSourceAdmin: I confirm the decision for this administrator of the source
mapping.confirmTargetAdmin: I confirm the mapping to an administrator of this instance
mapping.providerHint: Only this provider can claim the new account at the first sign-in.
mapping.confirmGuess: I confirm that this is the same person (matched by e-mail address or name only)

imports.title: Imports into this instance
imports.none: Nothing was imported into this instance.
imports.showHistory_one: Show the imported audit history ({{count}} entry)
imports.showHistory_other: Show the imported audit history ({{count}} entries)

look.title: Look of e-mails and Teams messages
look.intro: Name, colour, logo, footer and style of the messages Steward sends, and how dry runs are sent. Empty fields follow Settings → Appearance.
look.name: Name
look.nameHint: In the e-mail header, the subject and the Teams card. Empty: {{name}}
look.colorHint: Empty: the primary colour of the Appearance settings
look.colorInvalid: Use a hex colour like #1c7ed6, or leave it empty
look.eyeDropper: Pick a colour from the screen
look.logoHint: The logo travels inside the e-mail, so it shows without loading anything from Steward. Teams cards only carry logos up to 12 KB.

logoProblem.missing: No app logo is uploaded (Settings → Appearance): messages go out without a logo.
logoProblem.type: The app logo is a WebP image, which many mail clients cannot show: messages go out without a logo. Upload a PNG or JPEG, or use the report logo.
logoProblem.size: The logo is larger than 512 KB and is left out of messages.
logoProblem.missingCustom: No own logo is uploaded yet: messages go out without a logo until you upload one.

look.footerHint: Small print at the bottom of every e-mail and Teams card, e.g. “Internal – IT operations”
look.saved: Look of e-mails and Teams messages saved
look.testHint: Send a test under Notifications to see it in your mail client and in Teams.
look.subject: Subject: {{subject}}
look.previewTeamsHint: Teams draws the card itself; this shows its content, logo and colour strip.
look.customLogoHint: PNG or JPEG, at most 512 KB. Only for e-mails and Teams messages; the app and reports keep their logos.
look.logoTooLarge: The file is larger than 512 KB.
look.styleHint: E-mails follow all of these. Teams cards only take the logo size and position; Teams draws the rest itself.
look.dryRunHint: Messages about dry runs (a failed test run, a failed check in one) are marked as a test: “Dry run” in the subject, a grey banner “No action needed” and no red strip.

dryRunDelivery.marked: E-mail, Teams and webhook, marked as a test

backups.title: Backups
backups.card: Encrypted copies of the database and the data folder in an S3 bucket, kept by a retention rule and tested every week.
backups.intro: Steward copies its database and data folder on a schedule, encrypts the copy with your backup passphrase and uploads it to S3. Older copies are removed by the retention rule; once a week the newest copy is downloaded, decrypted and checked completely. Administrators are notified when a backup or a test fails.
backups.setup: Set a backup passphrase and choose the S3 storage (a platform with AWS request signing for the service s3), then turn on scheduled backups.

key.title: Backup passphrase
key.intro: Backups are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key from this passphrase. Steward keeps the key in its vault but never the passphrase. Write the passphrase down and keep it offline, apart from the master passphrase: without it nobody can read a backup – also not on a new server after a loss.
key.changeHint: After a change, new backups use the new passphrase. Backups made before stay readable with the passphrase they were made with – keep it until they are removed.

backups.storageHint: A platform whose sign-in is AWS request signing (SigV4) with the service s3; its base URL is the bucket.
backups.noStorage: No S3 platform yet – create one under Platforms.
backups.prefixHint: e.g. steward/ – letters, digits and . _ -, ending with /
backups.cronHint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday – default 02:15 every day
backups.retentionHint: The newest backup of each of the last days, weeks and months that have one; the newest backup is always kept. With S3 Object Lock, the bucket can also refuse deletes for a while.
backups.restoreTestHint: Download the newest backup, decrypt it, check every file, the database and the audit chain.
backups.noneStored: No backups in the bucket yet.

contents.title: Contents
contents.intro: A backup always holds the database, the vault, the audit anchor, the audit archives and the manifest – a restore needs them. Run artifacts, archived reports and evidence packs can be left out to keep backups small. All three are evidence: leave one out only when it is kept elsewhere.
contents.warningTitle: A restore from these backups lacks evidence
contents.warning: Left out: {{parts}}. Every backup names this in its manifest and its header (backup info), and the restore test shows it. Keep these files elsewhere, or include them again.

database.label: Database
database.lacks: Everything Steward stores: processes, runs, the catalogue, settings and the audit log.

vault.label: Vault (vault.json)
vault.lacks: The keys of the encrypted credentials – without it the database cannot be read.

auditAnchor.label: Audit anchor (audit-anchor.json)
auditAnchor.lacks: Shows that the audit log was not cut short.

auditArchives.label: Audit archives (audit-archives/)
auditArchives.lacks: Audit entries the audit retention moved out of the database.

records.label: Record attachments (records/)
records.lacks: Files attached to records and documents – originals.

branding.label: Branding (branding/)
branding.lacks: The logos of reports and messages.

artifacts.label: Run artifacts (artifacts/)
artifacts.lacks: Without it a restore lacks the screenshots, files and evidence of manual steps of every run. They cannot be made again; reports and evidence packs generated after the restore miss them.

reports.label: Archived reports (reports/)
reports.lacks: Without it a restore lacks the archived PDF reports. A report can be generated again from its run as a new version with another SHA-256; the archived copy and signatures added to it are gone – the audit log still names its SHA-256.

evidencePacks.label: Evidence packs (evidence-packs/)
evidencePacks.lacks: Without it a restore lacks the evidence packs built so far (they expire after their retention anyway). They can be built again for the same period, with a new signature, from the data still in Steward.

other.label: Other files
other.lacks: Everything else in the data folder.

exports.title: Exports
exports.card: Readable files of chosen data – cost plans, the plant registry, the catalogue, monitors, the audit log – written to S3 on a schedule, for sharing and archiving.
exports.intro: On a schedule, Steward writes readable files of the parts you choose to a folder in an S3 bucket – the backup's bucket or another one – with a manifest of their SHA-256 checksums.
exports.notForRestore: Exports are for sharing and archiving outside Steward, not for a restore – that is what backups are for. They run as the system and hold everything of their parts, so only administrators define them; they never hold secrets. Whoever can read the bucket can read readable exports.
exports.removeConfirm: Remove the export "{{name}}" and its history? Its files stay in the bucket.
exports.name: Name
exports.nameHint: Also the folder in the bucket: letters, digits and . _ -
exports.storageHint: A platform with AWS request signing (SigV4) for the service s3 – the backup's or another one.
exports.noStorage: No S3 platform yet – create one under Platforms.
exports.prefixHint: e.g. exports/ – each run writes to a subfolder named after the export and the UTC time
exports.cronHint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday – default 03:30 every Monday
exports.moduleOff: The module is switched off: this part is left out until it is on again.
exports.encrypt: Encrypt the files with the backup key
exports.encryptHint: Off (default): readable files – protect the bucket. On: every file, the manifest included, is encrypted like a backup and read with steward backup decrypt and the backup passphrase.
exports.encryptNoKey: Set the backup passphrase first (Settings → Backups).
exports.keepRunsHint: The files of older successful runs are removed from the bucket.
exports.pruned: Files removed by the retention rule

costPlans.label: Cost plans and entries
costPlans.description: The plan lines and the cost entries of every service for a fiscal year, as CSV (Costs module).

plant.label: Plant registry
plant.description: The whole registry in its import format (YAML or JSON) – it imports back unchanged (plant registry module).

services.label: Services
services.description: The service catalogue as CSV, archived services included.

applications.label: Applications
applications.description: The applications as CSV, archived ones included.

monitors.label: Monitors
monitors.description: Every monitor in its import format, one YAML document each (no heartbeat secrets).

auditLog.label: Audit log
auditLog.description: The audit entries of the last days, as CSV or JSON Lines.

scope.instance: Instance settings apply to the whole installation; administrators change them.
scope.personal: Your own settings (language, notifications, tokens) are on your profile.

security.title: Security & sign-in
security.description: How people sign in, where Steward may connect to, the public API, the MCP server, the vault and access tokens.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Ticket systems, Git sync, moving to another instance and the end-of-life source.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Channels and routes, how messages look, the daily summary and credential reminders.

appearance.title: Appearance & branding
appearance.description: Colours and logo of the app and of reports.

catalogue.title: Catalogue & compliance
catalogue.description: The CIA scale, scorecard rules, environments and compliance rules.

data.title: Data & retention
data.description: How long data is kept, storage, cleanup and backups.

assurance.title: Assurance policy
assurance.description: Where a second person (four-eyes) or a fresh confirmation (step-up) is required, the baseline, overrides and the assurance report.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Switch optional areas on or off (costs, data contracts, compliance, status pages and others), with how mature each one is; the plant registry and its map.

endOfLife.title: End of life
endOfLife.hint: Where release and support dates of products come from (endoflife.date), and how far ahead they warn.
